name: DeepTeam
description: DeepTeam is an open-source LLM red-teaming framework covering 120+ vulnerability types and 20+ single- and multi-turn attack methods, with mappings to OWASP, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS. Docs

name: PyRIT
description: PyRIT is Microsoft's Python Risk Identification Toolkit for generative AI, used by Microsoft's AI Red Team to automate adversarial probing with configurable targets, converters, scorers, and multi-turn orchestrators.

name: Confident AI
description: Confident AI is an AI quality platform for enterprise teams to standardize evals and observability, with native red teaming and AI governance gates that block releases failing vulnerability checks.

name: promptfoo red teaming
description: promptfoo's MIT-licensed red-teaming module scans applications for injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, and authorization flaws. OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire Promptfoo in March 2026. GitHub · Announcement

name: garak
description: garak, from NVIDIA, is a generative-AI red-teaming and vulnerability framework whose plugin architecture composes probes, generators, buffs, and detectors into automated attack runs. Paper

name: Giskard
description: Giskard is an open-source testing library for LLM agents and ML models whose scan automatically detects vulnerabilities including prompt injection, harmful content, hallucination, and sycophancy.

name: Moonshot
description: Moonshot, from the AI Verify Foundation, is a modular toolkit that combines benchmarking and red teaming of LLM applications behind a single API, CLI, and web UI.

name: Rogue
description: Rogue is a source-available AI-agent evaluation and red-teaming platform from Qualifire (Rogue Security); its proprietary license permits personal and internal use but requires separate licensing for commercial hosting.

name: Inspect AI
description: Inspect AI, from the UK AI Security Institute, is an evaluation framework whose solvers, scorers, and sandboxed tool use support safety and adversarial evaluations, including agentic attack scenarios. Docs

name: Agentic Security
description: Agentic Security is an open-source LLM vulnerability scanner and red-teaming CLI that fuzzes endpoints with jailbreak datasets, multi-step attacks, and stress tests.

name: FuzzyAI
description: FuzzyAI, from CyberArk, fuzzes LLM APIs with strategies including adversarial suffixes, genetic search, and encoding to identify jailbreaks and guardrail bypasses.

name: Prompt Fuzzer
description: Prompt Fuzzer, from Prompt Security (now a SentinelOne company), tests system prompts with prompt-injection and jailbreak attacks and scores the resulting resilience.

name: promptmap
description: promptmap is a prompt-injection scanner that tests a custom LLM application's system prompt with rule-based attack cases and reports which ones leak or override it.

name: spikee
description: spikee, from Reversec Labs, is a modular toolkit for testing LLMs, guardrails, and applications against prompt injection and jailbreak attacks and for generating targeted test datasets.

name: llm-attacks (GCG)
description: llm-attacks is the reference implementation of Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), which optimizes universal, transferable adversarial suffixes that jailbreak aligned models. Paper

name: PAIR
description: PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement) uses attacker, target, and judge models to iteratively refine jailbreak prompts in black-box settings. Paper

name: TAP
description: TAP (Tree of Attacks with Pruning) extends PAIR with tree-of-thought search and pruning to jailbreak black-box models query-efficiently. Paper

name: AutoDAN
description: AutoDAN generates stealthy, human-readable jailbreak prompts via a hierarchical genetic algorithm, evading perplexity-based filters that catch gradient suffixes. Paper

name: GPTFuzz
description: GPTFuzz is a black-box jailbreak fuzzer that mutates human-written seed templates and uses a judge model to grow an attack corpus automatically. Paper

name: EasyJailbreak
description: EasyJailbreak provides a common interface for implementing, constructing, and evaluating multiple jailbreak methods. Paper

name: DeepInception
description: DeepInception is a prompt-only jailbreak that nests a model inside layered fictional scenarios to erode its safety guardrails. Paper

name: PromptInject
description: PromptInject is the framework accompanying the "Ignore Previous Prompt" paper, quantifying goal hijacking and prompt leaking via mask-based iterative adversarial prompt composition. Paper

name: ArtPrompt
description: ArtPrompt is an ASCII-art-based jailbreak that hides unsafe words in text art to bypass token-level safety filters. Paper

name: Open-Prompt-Injection
description: Open-Prompt-Injection is a research framework implementing standardized prompt-injection attacks and defenses for reproducible evaluation. Paper

name: BIPIA
description: BIPIA, from Microsoft, benchmarks indirect prompt injection across email QA, web QA, table QA, summarization, and code QA, with black-box and white-box defense baselines. Paper

name: HouYi
description: HouYi is a black-box prompt-injection attack framework that systematically composes a framework, separator, and disruptor to hijack LLM-integrated applications. Paper

name: Tensor Trust
description: Tensor Trust is a prompt-injection attack-and-defense game from UC Berkeley whose gameplay produced a public dataset of human-crafted injections and defenses. Paper

name: deepset prompt-injections
description: The deepset prompt-injections dataset is an Apache-2.0 labeled corpus of injection and benign prompts for training and evaluating injection classifiers.

name: Lakera PINT Benchmark
description: PINT (Prompt Injection Test), from Lakera, provides a dataset and harness for evaluating prompt-injection detectors without training on the test set.

name: Adversarial Robustness Toolbox
description: ART, from the Linux Foundation AI & Data (originally IBM), provides evasion, poisoning, extraction, and inference attacks and defenses for multiple machine-learning frameworks and data modalities.

name: Foolbox
description: Foolbox creates adversarial examples against PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX models using gradient-based, decision-based, and score-based attacks.

name: CleverHans
description: CleverHans provides reference adversarial-example attack implementations for benchmarking model robustness.

name: TextAttack
description: TextAttack is a framework for adversarial attacks, data augmentation, and adversarial training in NLP, with many recipe-based text attacks.

name: OpenAttack
description: OpenAttack, from THUNLP, is a textual adversarial attack toolkit supporting sentence-, word-, and character-level attacks and attack evaluation.

name: AdvBox
description: AdvBox, from Baidu, is a toolbox for generating adversarial examples and testing the robustness of models across multiple deep-learning frameworks.

name: Armory
description: Armory, from Two Six Technologies, is an adversarial-ML evaluation testbed built for the DARPA GARD program, orchestrating scenario-based robustness experiments.

name: Check Point AI Red Teaming
description: Check Point AI Red Teaming, built from the Lakera acquisition, runs adversarial assessments against models and agents and draws attack intelligence from the Gandalf community.

name: Mindgard
description: Mindgard is an automated AI red-teaming and offensive-security platform that maps attack surfaces and continuously tests models, agents, applications, and infrastructure.

name: HiddenLayer
description: HiddenLayer provides automated red teaming and attack simulation for generative, agentic, and predictive AI, alongside model scanning and runtime detection and response.

name: Agent Torture Lab
description: Agent Torture Lab is a commercial AI-agent testing service that probes customer-support bots for policy, privacy, and escalation failures and returns evidence-linked transcripts with a fix plan and retest plan.

name: Cisco AI Defense
description: Cisco AI Defense, built on the Robust Intelligence acquisition, provides algorithmic red teaming and runtime guardrails for enterprise AI applications.

name: Haize Labs
description: Haize Labs builds domain-specific agents with a proprietary Reliability Harness that combines simulation testing, adversarial red teaming, guardrails, and evaluation judges.

name: Prisma AIRS AI Red Teaming
description: Prisma AIRS AI Red Teaming, incorporating technology from Palo Alto Networks' Protect AI acquisition, runs adaptive adversarial assessments against AI applications and agents.

name: Adversa AI
description: Adversa AI provides continuous red teaming, threat modeling, and remediation for custom AI agents, applications, models, APIs, and MCP-connected infrastructure.

name: F5 AI Red Team
description: F5 AI Red Team, built from the CalypsoAI acquisition, uses adversarial agents to test models and applications for prompt injection, jailbreaks, and other AI-specific vulnerabilities.

name: Zscaler Automated AI Red Teaming
description: Zscaler Automated AI Red Teaming, built from the SPLX acquisition, continuously tests GenAI applications with customizable probes and integrates findings into development and governance workflows.

name: Enkrypt AI
description: Enkrypt AI offers automated red teaming, risk assessment, and guardrails for LLM applications, with compliance-oriented reporting.

name: Gray Swan Shade
description: Shade runs adaptive adversarial campaigns against models, agents, guardrails, and deployment contexts using attack intelligence from Gray Swan's Arena research environment.

name: Repello AI ARTEMIS
description: ARTEMIS is Repello AI's automated red-teaming engine for continuous adversarial testing of LLM applications, RAG pipelines, and agentic systems, with CI/CD integration.

name: Patronus AI
description: Patronus AI's evaluation platform supports OWASP-aligned adversarial datasets, custom attack generation, evaluators, and simulated environments for testing AI models and agents.

name: NeMo Guardrails
description: NeMo Guardrails is NVIDIA's toolkit for programmable guardrails (via Colang) on conversational systems, with topic control, jailbreak detection, and fact-checking rails.

name: Guardrails AI
description: Guardrails AI is a Python framework for input/output validation, with a community Guardrails Hub of validators for injection, PII, and toxicity.

name: LlamaFirewall
description: LlamaFirewall, from Meta, is an open-source guardrail framework for agentic systems that combines PromptGuard, agent-alignment checks, and code-safety scanning.

name: Invariant Guardrails
description: Invariant Guardrails is an Apache-2.0 rule-based layer for agentic systems that enforces policies over messages and tool calls; Snyk acquired Invariant Labs in 2025.

name: Llama Guard
description: Llama Guard is Meta's family of downloadable safety-classifier models for input and output moderation, released under Meta's community license as part of Purple Llama.

name: Prompt Guard
description: Prompt Guard, from Meta, is an 86M-parameter downloadable classifier that flags prompt-injection and jailbreak strings in user inputs and retrieved content.

name: ShieldGemma
description: ShieldGemma, from Google, is a family of Gemma-based safety-classifier models for filtering harmful content in prompts and responses.

name: Granite Guardian
description: Granite Guardian, from IBM, is an Apache-2.0 family of downloadable guardrail models for detecting harm, jailbreaks, and RAG groundedness and relevance risks.

name: Check Point AI Agent Security
description: Check Point AI Agent Security, formerly Lakera Guard, enforces runtime policies across prompts, responses, external content, and agent tool calls.

name: Azure AI Content Safety
description: Azure AI Content Safety provides content moderation plus Prompt Shields for direct and indirect prompt attacks, groundedness detection, and agent task-adherence checks.

name: Google Model Armor
description: Model Armor is Google Cloud's service for screening LLM prompts and responses for injection, jailbreaks, sensitive data, malicious URLs, and harmful content.

name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
description: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applies configurable safety policies — content filters, denied topics, and contextual grounding checks — to Bedrock applications.

name: OpenAI Moderation
description: The OpenAI Moderation endpoint is a free hosted API for text and image safety classification.

name: AgentDojo
description: AgentDojo, from ETH Zurich, is a dynamic environment for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defenses against tool-using LLM agents on realistic tasks. Paper

name: InjecAgent
description: InjecAgent is a benchmark for indirect prompt-injection attacks against tool-integrated agents, measuring both direct harm and data-exfiltration outcomes. Paper

name: Agent Security Bench
description: Agent Security Bench (ASB) formalizes and benchmarks a broad range of attacks and defenses on LLM agents, including direct/indirect injection, memory poisoning, and backdoors. Paper

name: ToolEmu
description: ToolEmu uses an LLM to emulate tool execution so agents can be stress-tested for risky behavior in high-stakes scenarios without real side effects. Paper

name: Agentic Radar
description: Agentic Radar, created by SPLX before its Zscaler acquisition, maps an agentic workflow's tools and dependencies and probes it for security weaknesses.

name: AgentHarm
description: AgentHarm, from the UK AI Security Institute and Gray Swan AI, measures harmful multi-step agent behavior and jailbreak transfer; its license restricts use to improving AI safety and security. Paper

name: JailbreakBench
description: JailbreakBench is an open robustness benchmark for jailbreaking, with a standardized dataset, evaluation pipeline, leaderboard, and artifact repository. Paper

name: HarmBench
description: HarmBench provides a standardized set of harmful behaviors and a validation classifier for comparing attack success and refusal robustness across methods. Paper

name: StrongREJECT
description: StrongREJECT pairs forbidden prompts with an autograder that scores refusal, specificity, and convincingness to measure whether a jailbreak produces actionable harmful content. Paper

name: JailbreakV-28K
description: JailbreakV-28K contains 20,000 text-based transfer attacks and 8,000 image-based attacks for testing jailbreak robustness in multimodal large language models. Paper

name: SORRY-Bench
description: SORRY-Bench evaluates refusal behavior with 440 balanced instructions across 44 unsafe topics and 20 linguistic augmentations. Paper

name: h4rm3l
description: h4rm3l is a domain-specific language and benchmark for composing novel jailbreak attacks programmatically and measuring their success. Paper

name: AILuminate
description: AILuminate is MLCommons' safety-benchmark family covering 12 hazard categories. Its Apache-2.0 repository provides an offline demo; practice and official tests use separately licensed or confidential prompt sets. Website

name: DecodingTrust
description: DecodingTrust assesses toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness (NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper). Paper

name: TrustLLM
description: TrustLLM benchmarks trustworthiness across truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics. Paper

name: SafetyBench
description: SafetyBench is a multiple-choice LLM safety evaluation across seven harm categories in English and Chinese. Paper

name: Do-Not-Answer
description: Do-Not-Answer is a dataset of questions responsible models should refuse, with an evaluation protocol for safeguard effectiveness. Paper

name: XSTest
description: XSTest tests exaggerated safety (over-refusal) using safe prompts that superficially resemble unsafe ones. Paper

name: ToxiGen
description: ToxiGen is a publicly downloadable dataset of synthetic implicit toxic and benign statements mentioning 13 minority groups; its dataset card specifies no license, and Microsoft has archived the original code repository. Code · Paper

name: WMDP
description: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy) measures hazardous knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemistry as a proxy for dangerous capabilities. Paper

name: CyberSecEval
description: CyberSecEval, part of Meta's Purple Llama project, benchmarks cybersecurity risks and capabilities including insecure code generation, prompt injection, cyberattack helpfulness, and defensive tasks.

name: SALAD-Bench
description: SALAD-Bench is a hierarchical safety benchmark for LLMs, attacks, and defenses, paired with an MD-Judge evaluator across a structured harm taxonomy. Paper

name: BeaverTails
description: BeaverTails, from PKU-Alignment, is a QA dataset with separate helpfulness and harmlessness annotations for safety alignment research. Paper

name: In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts
description: In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts collects 15,000+ jailbreak prompts, including DAN-family prompts, from public platforms for studying attacks observed in practice. Paper

name: AdvBench
description: AdvBench is the harmful-behaviors and harmful-strings dataset introduced with GCG as a target set for jailbreak research. Paper

name: HackAPrompt Dataset
description: HackAPrompt contains 600,000+ adversarial prompts submitted to a global prompt-hacking competition; the MIT-licensed dataset requires accepting Hugging Face access conditions. Paper

name: HarmfulQA
description: HarmfulQA, from DeCLaRe Lab, is an Apache-2.0 dataset of harmful questions and red-teaming conversations created with the Chain of Utterances method. Paper

name: ToxicChat
description: ToxicChat, from LMSYS, contains toxicity and jailbreak labels for real user queries to a chatbot; prompts and outputs are licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0. Paper

name: MM-SafetyBench
description: MM-SafetyBench evaluates multimodal-LLM safety against query-relevant image-based jailbreaks; its dataset is restricted to noncommercial research under CC-BY-NC-4.0. Paper

name: ForbiddenQuestions
description: ForbiddenQuestions pairs policy-violating questions with jailbreak prompts to measure attack success across scenarios. Paper

name: ModelScan
category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
description: ModelScan scans model files, including pickle, HDF5, and SavedModel formats, for code that executes on load and other model-serialization threats.

name: picklescan
category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
description: picklescan analyzes Python pickle files for suspicious imports and opcodes, and is integrated into Hugging Face Hub's malware scanning.

name: Fickling
category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
description: Fickling, from Trail of Bits, is a decompiler, static analyzer, and bytecode rewriter for pickle files, used to detect and craft malicious payloads for testing.

name: safetensors
category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
description: safetensors is a safe serialization format for model weights that avoids the arbitrary-code-execution behavior of pickle-based checkpoints.

name: HiddenLayer Model Scanner
category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
description: HiddenLayer's Model Scanner statically inspects model artifacts for malware, backdoors, and integrity issues before they enter production.

name: Prisma AIRS AI Model Security
category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
description: Prisma AIRS AI Model Security, incorporating Protect AI technology, scans model architecture, weights, operators, dependencies, and embedded code before deployment.

name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
description: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications is a community-maintained risk list covering prompt injection, sensitive-information disclosure, supply-chain weaknesses, and other GenAI application risks.

name: MITRE ATLAS
description: MITRE ATLAS is an ATT&CK-style knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against AI systems, backed by real-world case studies.

name: OWASP ML Security Top 10
description: The OWASP Machine Learning Security Top 10 catalogs risks to classic ML systems, such as data poisoning and model inversion.

name: AI Vulnerability Database
description: AVID is a public database and taxonomy of AI failure modes and vulnerabilities, providing a common reporting schema for the community.

name: AI Incident Database
description: The AI Incident Database, from the Responsible AI Collaborative, indexes reported real-world AI harms and near-misses to inform threat modeling.

name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
description: The NIST AI RMF is a voluntary U.S. framework for governing AI risk, with a Generative AI profile addressing risks specific to generative systems.

name: Google Secure AI Framework (SAIF)
description: SAIF is Google's published conceptual framework and risk map for securing AI systems across the development and deployment lifecycle.

name: Counterfit
description: Counterfit remains public and unarchived, but its latest release dates to November 2022 and its latest functional code changes to April 2023; PyRIT is Microsoft's current generative-AI red-teaming framework.

name: LLMFuzzer
description: LLMFuzzer's maintainers explicitly mark the project as unmaintained and invite users to fork it.

name: Vigil
description: Vigil is not formally archived, but its latest release was in December 2023, its latest code update was in January 2024, and its README describes it as alpha research software.

name: Rebuff
description: Protect AI archived Rebuff in May 2025; the repository remains available under Apache-2.0.

name: LLM Guard
description: Protect AI archived LLM Guard in July 2026 and states that the project and associated models are no longer developed or maintained.

name: Robust Intelligence
description: Cisco acquired Robust Intelligence in October 2024; its algorithmic red teaming is now part of Cisco AI Defense.

name: Prompt Security
description: SentinelOne completed its acquisition of Prompt Security in 2025; Prompt Security now operates within the SentinelOne Singularity platform.

name: Protect AI
description: Palo Alto Networks acquired Protect AI in July 2025 and integrated its model scanning, red teaming, and runtime technology into Prisma AIRS.

name: CalypsoAI
description: F5 announced its agreement to acquire CalypsoAI in September 2025; F5 now describes F5 AI Red Team and F5 AI Guardrails as generally available products stemming from the acquisition.

name: SPLX
description: Zscaler acquired SPLX in November 2025 and integrated its discovery, automated red teaming, and governance technology into Zscaler AI Security.

name: Lakera
description: Check Point completed its acquisition of Lakera in October 2025; Lakera Red and Lakera Guard were succeeded by Check Point AI Red Teaming and AI Agent Security.

name: Invariant Labs
description: Snyk acquired Invariant Labs in June 2025; the Apache-2.0 Invariant Guardrails repository remains public while its technology contributes to Snyk's AI security products and research.
